title: Foxconn third-quarter revenue soars on AI demand, beats market forecast
source_used: Reuters text on The Economic Times (full Reuters wire text); The Star (Reuters) and Yahoo Finance versions agree on the figures. Reuters original not opened (HTTP 401).
key_facts: Taiwan's Foxconn, the world's largest contract electronics maker, reported on Monday 5 Oct 2026 a 47% jump in July-September revenue from a year earlier, fuelled by strong AI-related demand.
Revenue was T$3.03 trillion ($95.4 billion), well above an LSEG SmartEstimate of T$2.83 trillion (which gives more weight to analysts who are more consistently accurate).
Strong AI demand drove robust growth in the cloud and networking products division; smart consumer electronics, which include iPhones, also grew significantly.
September revenue alone rose 38% to T$1.16 trillion, a record month and the first above T$1 trillion.

Foxconn expects AI-related operations to keep growing in the fourth quarter and, with the seasonal peak, to 'support overall performance in line with current market expectations', but says it must monitor a volatile global political and economic environment.
Foxconn (formally Hon Hai Precision Industry) gives no numerical forecasts and will report full third-quarter earnings on 12 November.
Reuters (The Star version): Foxconn is also Nvidia's biggest server maker.
quote_evidence: Taiwan's Foxconn, the world's largest contract electronics maker, reported on Monday a 47% jump in third-quarter revenue year-on-year that beat market estimates, fuelled by strong AI-related demand.

Revenue for the July-September quarter was T$3.03 trillion ($95.4 billion), well above an LSEG SmartEstimate of T$2.83 trillion that gives greater weight to forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate.
September revenue alone rose 38% year-on-year to T$1.16 trillion, a record for a single month and the first time it has surpassed T$1 trillion on a monthly basis.
why_it_matters_hint: Foxconn builds AI servers for Nvidia, so its sales are an early read on AI hardware demand.
